tool.name: Build haplotype sheet
tool.description: collect window haplotype calls into a PyEuk sheet, keeping read frequency
tool.command: ## Reduces the whole collection: the sheet only means anything across specimens. ## Element identifiers are sanitised into filenames, but the specimen id itself is ## read from each file's own 'specimen' column, never from the filename. mkdir -p calls && #import re #for $c in $calls_in ln -s '$c' 'calls/${re.sub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", str($c.element_identifier))}.tsv' && #end for pyeuk build-sheet calls out --min-freq $min_freq --min-reads $min_reads --min-maf $min_maf

param.label: Extra haplotype-frequency filter
param.help: Minimum haplotype frequency to keep a call.

param.label: Extra minimum reads per haplotype
param.help: Minimum supporting reads to keep a call.

param.label: Minor-allele filter
param.help: Drop a column unless the fraction of called specimens carrying it is between this value and 1 minus it. 0 disables. The fraction is over specimens, not reads.

data.name: dropped
data.label: ${tool.name}: columns removed by the minor-allele filter

tool.help:
Compiles the per-specimen haplotype calls into a binary specimen-by-haplotype matrix and a long-format read-frequency table. The point is to decouple allelic presence from observational absence, so that a technical locus dropout is treated as missing data, not as identity with the reference.
Specimens are rows and distinct window-haplotypes are columns. ``X`` marks presence. Every column of a window is left empty when the locus was NOT_CALLED. Reference-identical alleles are tracked explicitly under ``=``, so a reference match and a dropout are different cells. The long-format table records absolute read counts and within-host frequencies for every called variant, preserving mixture proportions the binary matrix cannot hold.
Cohort-wide minor-allele filtering (``min_maf``) is off by default (0.0). An arbitrary threshold removes informative rare outbreak markers. @HELP_FOOTER@
